thread:
Anya: Quick sync—need to trim OBS scope for Q2. Customers are pushing hard for per-tenant cost and faster tracing hooks. How should we prioritize?
Devon: We can't do full per-tenant cost + live heatmaps in Q2. My vote: per-tenant daily reporting + compact dashboards first. Keep live/real-time as a follow-up.
Ravi: +1. For tracing hooks we can add an ingress span tag to correlate requests without full tracing. Sampling policy is the lever here — propose default 1%, 5% for enterprise tenants.
Maya: From enterprise POV: per-tenant SLA breach alerts + cost attribution are blockers for their adoption. They want near-real-time billing for chargebacks, but we can accept a daily rollup if we promise roadmap.
Ben: Proposed split (must-have / nice-to-have):
  - Must-have: per-tenant daily cost aggregates, trace ingress tag, sampling + canary at 1%
  - Nice-to-have: live heatmap, per-token UI cost breakdown, trace span waterfall viewer
Anya: Launch criteria suggestion: must-have implemented + e2e acceptance tests + docs + rollout plan. Canary gates: error delta < 2% vs baseline, p99 latency increase < 10%.
Devon: Implementation note: reuse billing pipeline, add tenant_id tag at ingestion, compute daily aggregates with existing job. Dashboard surfaces: time-range, compare, and tenant filter.
Ravi: Sampling config prototype:
```
sampling:
  default: 0.01
  enterprise_overrides:
    tenant_alpha: 0.05
    tenant_beta: 0.05
```
This keeps overhead low but gives more signal for paying customers.
Maya: Security: for tenants that request it, tenant_id in traces must be pseudonymized/hashed before export. Also call out retention and access controls in the PRD.
Ben: Rollout plan: internal beta -> 2 x enterprise customers -> GA. Use a feature flag + canary-bot to auto-stop if canary metrics breach thresholds.
canary-bot: Canary scheduled: week-of-May-15. Monitoring hooks configured: cost_delta, error_rate, p99_latency. Alerts to #eng-oncall and product.
Anya: Owners: @Devon owns instrumentation + acceptance tests, @Maya owns enterprise requirements & compliance checklist, @Ravi owns sampling/runtime configs.
Devon: I'll own instrumentation and acceptance tests. ETA: 3 sprints (assuming infra slot).
Maya: I'll draft enterprise requirements doc and compliance checklist, include pseudonymization options.
Ravi: I'll add sampling rollout config and run a small perf bench. Need eng-sre to reserve infra windows.
Tom (SRE): FYI we need to reserve infra for the canary—recommend 48h of representative traffic and capacity for burst.
Anya: Decision: proceed with Ben's must-have split. I'll synthesize a compact PRD and ticket list by EOD, and schedule a follow-up sync to confirm infra windows. :thumbsup:
